questions.question: When turning to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do not brake. Braking can lock your wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not brake. Braking can lock your wheels.
questions.explanation: Do not brake while turning quickly to avoid a hazard. Braking can cause your wheels to lock and make your vehicle skid out of control.

questions.question: When a bus is stopped at a railroad crossing, how can the driver hear if a train is coming?

options.text: Wait for passengers to be quiet on their own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the front door.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing, the driver should stop 15 to 50 feet from the tracks. They should look both ways and open the front door to help see or hear a train coming.

questions.question: On the basic control skills test, when do you receive points?

options.text: When you cross the exercise boundary lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you cross the exercise boundary lines.
questions.explanation: The examiner counts how many times your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line. Each time counts as an error against your score.

questions.question: Most heavy trucks with manual transmissions need ____ to change gears.
questions.correctAnswerText: Double clutching
questions.explanation: Most heavy trucks with manual transmissions require double clutching to shift gears. This skill takes practice to master.

questions.question: When should you do an after-trip inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: After every trip.
questions.explanation: Always do an after-trip inspection at the end of each trip, day, or shift. Fill out a vehicle inspection report if required.

questions.question: If there is a cargo fire in a box trailer, what should you do?

options.text: Do not open the trailer doors.
Put a heavy blanket over the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not open the trailer doors.
questions.explanation: Do not open trailer doors during a cargo fire. Opening them adds oxygen to the fire, which makes it grow larger. This is especially important if the cargo contains hazardous materials.

questions.question: What helps you stay alert while driving?

options.text: Eat a heavy meal before starting your trip.
Drive with a second person who can take turns driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with a second person who can take turns driving.
questions.explanation: Having a second driver reduces the risk that either driver will get tired. You can also stay alert by avoiding heavy foods and keeping the cab cool.

questions.question: If your vehicle catches fire, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Park away from buildings, trees, brush, and other vehicles.
Call emergency services and tell them where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull into a service station.
questions.explanation: Leave the road and stop in an open area. Do not go to a service station because fuel there could catch fire. Call emergency services and give them your location.

questions.question: When starting from a complete stop, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle should shift to the right.
The vehicle should go into third gear.
The vehicle should not roll backward.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle should not roll backward.
questions.explanation: Make sure your vehicle does not roll backward when starting from a complete stop. This prevents hitting anything behind you.

questions.question: When parking in an offset back/left space, what should you do?

options.text: Go forward straight, then back up to the left.
Back up straight, then go forward to the left.
Go forward straight, then back up straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go forward straight, then back up to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, first go straight forward, then back up to the left. Your vehicle must stay completely within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: When parking parallel on the driver's side, what should you do?

options.text: Drive straight into the parking space.
Back up past the space, then drive forward into it.
Drive past the space, then back into it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive past the space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space first. Then back your vehicle into it. Keep the rear of your vehicle close to the rear of the space. Your vehicle must fit completely within the space.

questions.question: Why is watching the road ahead important?

options.text: It gives you time to plan how to avoid hazards.
It only matters in heavy traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to plan how to avoid hazards.
questions.explanation: Always watch the road ahead. This gives you time to react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: Where are regrooved tires allowed on a bus?
questions.correctAnswerText: Only on the rear.
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires are not allowed on the front of a bus.

questions.question: How does a smaller vehicle compare to your vehicle when stopping?

options.text: It usually stops faster than your vehicle.
It usually takes longer to stop than your vehicle.
It takes about the same time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It usually stops faster than your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Smaller vehicles can stop faster than larger vehicles. Remember this when deciding how far to stay behind other vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do when the examiner asks you to change lanes?

options.text: Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
Change lanes quickly, even if you cut off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Check traffic around you and use your turn signal before changing lanes. Only change lanes when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: How does a tired driver compare to a normal driver?

options.text: They are usually more careful than other drivers.
They may be slower to make critical decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may be slower to make critical decisions.
questions.explanation: Tired drivers are slower to see or react to hazards. They have a harder time making important decisions while driving.

questions.question: Should dual tires touch each other?

options.text: Yes, they should touch fairly often.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, they should not touch.
questions.explanation: When inspecting your vehicle, make sure dual tires do not touch each other or any other part of the vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do on long driving trips?
questions.correctAnswerText: Take rest breaks.
questions.explanation: Take a break every 100 miles or every two hours of driving. Avoid driving at night or when you would normally be asleep, as this increases the risk of becoming tired.

questions.question: If you must drive slowly and block traffic, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Use your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly and block traffic, turn on your four-way flashers to warn drivers behind you (if local laws allow).

questions.question: What is true about broken suspension parts?
questions.correctAnswerText: They are very dangerous.
questions.explanation: The suspension system supports the vehicle and its load and keeps the axles in place. Broken parts in this system are very dangerous.
